summary: Recent updates to the 2D graphics library in Firefox focused on enhancing the accuracy and reliability of image processing. Changes included making the unpremultiplication process—used to manage transparency in images—more precise across different hardware configurations, including Intel and ARM devices. The library also now gracefully handles failures when inflating source rectangles, ensuring that errors do not disrupt the rendering process. Additionally, developers cleaned up the code by removing obsolete components and improved software filters by clamping float parameters, leading to better visual consistency. Overall, these enhancements contribute to more robust graphics handling, which is essential for a smoother and more reliable browsing experience. **Users can expect improved image quality and stability when viewing graphics-heavy content.**
